scope.purpose: Operationalize ISO 19650-2:2018 5.3.6 by establishing the delivery team's risks to timely information delivery and the intended management response.
scope.boundary: This workflow governs information-delivery risk for the tender response. It may reference a wider project risk register but does not treat generic project risk capture as sufficient unless the required information-delivery risks and responses are traceable.

risk_groups.description: Assumptions made by the delivery team in relation to the appointing party's exchange information requirements.
Risks to meeting the appointing party's project information delivery milestones.
Risks arising from the contents or application of the project's information protocol.
Risks to achieving the proposed information delivery strategy.
Risks in adopting the project's information standard and information production methods and procedures.
Risks associated with inclusion or non-inclusion of proposed amendments to the project's information standard.
Risks in mobilizing the delivery team to achieve required capability and capacity.

risk_record_contract.rule: A risk group with no identified risk shall record the assessment basis; silence is not evidence that the group was considered.

process.rule: Resolve the ISO function through project evidence; do not infer it from a TIVERIT title.
Evaluate every 5.3.6 risk group and preserve assumptions and dependencies.
For each identified risk record how it can affect timely delivery in accordance with the EIR.
Record how the delivery team intends to manage each identified risk, including responsibility and evidence/dependency references.
The information-delivery risk register may be incorporated into another project risk register only if these records remain identifiable and traceable.

conformance_rules.rule: All seven 5.3.6 risk groups shall be demonstrably evaluated.
Every identified information-delivery risk shall include an intended management response.
A generic project risk register shall not satisfy 5.3.6 unless the information-delivery risks are identifiable and traceable to the required risk groups.
Unresolved EIR assumptions shall not be silently normalized into confirmed project facts.
The actor establishing the register shall be mapped to the prospective lead appointed party through project evidence.
